I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over four decades. I know exactly what it needs. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

**My land split:** My wheat-maize rotation runs on about 7 mu — same field, two crops a year. The remaining 3.1 mu I keep in cotton for cash income. My household is just two of us now, so I can't go overboard on labor-intensive practices.

**Wheat (this coming autumn, harvested next summer):** I'll use improved varieties — something like Jimai 22 or a local elite line I trust. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest in late September, apply base fertilizer, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. Three irrigations: once at sowing to establish the seedbed, once at jointing, once at heading. The groundwater table under Quzhou keeps dropping — I've watched it my whole life — so I won't waste water. Two pesticide passes: one for aphids in spring, one fungicide for rust or powdery mildew.

**Maize (summer, after wheat):** I direct-seed hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 has served me well for years. No tillage, just clean up the wheat stubble and seed straight in. I'll sidedress nitrogen at the V6 stage and again at tasseling. Maybe two irrigations if July rains are short. One pesticide application for corn borer if pressure is high.

**Cotton (spring through autumn):** I plough this plot in April, work in a good base fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium. Cotton eats potassium, and I know what happens when I skimp. I'll irrigate four times across the long season. The real work is pest management — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I plan five pesticide applications, spaced through the season. The market for cotton has been soft, but 3.1 mu is manageable and diversifies my income.
